description: List connected displays with their current layout (resolution, position, rotation, scaling) and each display's index, the display_index macos_take_screenshot and macos_manage_windows use, or apply a pre-configured display layout by name. Requires displayplacer CLI (brew install displayplacer). Layouts are pre-configured in the MACOS_DISPLAY_LAYOUTS environment variable as a JSON object mapping names to displayplacer argument strings; action=list returns their names as layouts. Layout application only accepts named presets — raw displayplacer args are never accepted from the user.

action.description: list — enumerate connected displays; apply_layout — activate a saved layout.

layout_name.description: Name of the display layout to apply for action=apply_layout: one of the names action=list returns as layouts.

name: macos_manage_displays

current_config.description: The current displayplacer command that would reproduce the active arrangement. Present for action=list.

displays.description: Connected display inventory. Present for action=list.

items.description: Connected display with its current layout configuration.

enabled.description: True when the display is active or part of a mirroring set, so a display mirroring another reads true; false when it is disabled.

hz.description: Refresh rate, e.g. "60"; "N/A" when macOS reports none.

id.description: Persistent display identifier assigned by macOS.

index.description: 0-based position in macOS's screen list (NSScreen.screens), where 0 is the main display: the display_index macos_take_screenshot captures and macos_manage_windows reports. null when the display has no screen in that list, such as a disabled display. Absent only when the screen list could not be read; notice says why.

origin.description: Position origin in the global display arrangement, e.g. "(0,0)".

type.description: How displayplacer describes the display: "MacBook built in screen" for a built-in panel, "<N> inch external screen" (the diagonal) for any other.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `displayplacer_not_found`: The displayplacer CLI is not on PATH or in either Homebrew bin directory (/opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin). `displayplacer_output_unrecognized`: displayplacer list printed a display block missing one of the lines this server reads (Persistent screen id, Contextual screen id, Type, Resolution, Hertz, Scaling, Origin, Rotation, Enabled) or carrying a Contextual screen id or Enabled value displayplacer never prints, or printed no arrangement command. `layout_not_found`: layout_name is not one of the layout names configured in MACOS_DISPLAY_LAYOUTS. `layouts_invalid`: action=apply_layout while MACOS_DISPLAY_LAYOUTS is not a JSON object mapping layout names to non-empty displayplacer argument strings. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

layout_name.description: Name of the layout that was applied. Present for action=apply_layout.

layouts.description: Names of the layouts configured in MACOS_DISPLAY_LAYOUTS; [] when none are. Present for action=list, except when MACOS_DISPLAY_LAYOUTS is invalid (notice says why).

items.description: A layout name, usable as layout_name for action=apply_layout.

notice.description: Present for action=list when index or layouts could not be read: names what failed and what to do.

success.description: True when the layout was applied. Present for action=apply_layout.

title: Manage macOS Displays
